error_message: TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'userId')
root_cause: JWT token expired silently — req.user was null because the token verification middleware wasn't re-checking token expiry on refresh. The session was cached in Redis with the old token.
fix_applied: Added explicit token expiry check in auth.js line 47. Cleared Redis session cache with: redis-cli FLUSHDB. Added a 401 response handler on the frontend to auto-logout on token expiry.

error_message: sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (psycopg2.OperationalError) FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections
root_cause: PostgreSQL max_connections limit hit (default 100). The connection pool was not being released properly because async context managers were not used — raw session.close() was missing in exception paths.
fix_applied: Switched from raw sessions to async context managers (async with SessionLocal() as db). Set pool_size=10, max_overflow=20 in SQLAlchemy engine config. Added pgbouncer as connection pooler in production.

error_message: AssertionError: Expected user balance to be 500, got 350
root_cause: Race condition in concurrent payment processing — two simultaneous requests both read the same balance before either write committed. Classic read-modify-write race with no DB-level locking.
fix_applied: Replaced optimistic update with SELECT FOR UPDATE in the transaction query. Used database-level row locking: db.query(User).filter(User.id == user_id).with_for_update().first(). Added integration test with concurrent requests using asyncio.gather.

error_message: FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
root_cause: Event listeners were being added inside a loop without cleanup. Each job run added a new 'data' listener to the stream without removing the old one — classic Node.js memory leak pattern.
fix_applied: Moved event listener outside the loop. Added stream.removeAllListeners('data') at the end of each job. Used --max-old-space-size=4096 as temporary workaround. Added memory monitoring with process.memoryUsage() logged every 60 seconds.

error_message: Access to XMLHttpRequest blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header
root_cause: CORS middleware was added AFTER the route definitions in FastAPI. FastAPI middleware order matters — CORS must be added before routes are registered, or preflight OPTIONS requests fail silently.
fix_applied: Moved app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, ...) to the top of main.py, before any @app.include_router() calls. Also added 'OPTIONS' to allowed_methods explicitly.

error_message: KeyError: 'session_token' / Cache miss causing 500 on every 15th request
root_cause: Redis session TTL was set to 900 seconds (15 min) but the frontend polling interval was 16 minutes. Every session expired between polls, causing a cache miss that wasn't handled gracefully — it raised a raw KeyError instead of returning a 401.
fix_applied: Added try/except around Redis GET with fallback to DB lookup. Changed TTL to 3600 seconds. Added cache-aside pattern: check Redis → miss → query DB → repopulate Redis. Added metric logging for cache hit/miss ratio.

error_message: requests.exceptions.ConnectionError: HTTPConnectionPool(host='db', port=5432): Max retries exceeded
root_cause: Service startup order in docker-compose — the app container started before the postgres container was ready to accept connections. depends_on only waits for container start, not for PostgreSQL to be fully ready.
fix_applied: Added healthcheck to postgres service in docker-compose.yml. Added depends_on condition: service_healthy for the app service. Also added a retry loop in app startup with exponential backoff (3 retries, 2s delay).

root_cause: Blocking I/O call (pandas read_csv on a 500MB file) inside an async def route handler — this blocked the entire event loop. All other requests queued behind it.
fix_applied: Wrapped the blocking pandas call with asyncio.to_thread(pd.read_csv, filepath). For very large files, switched to chunked reading with chunksize=10000. Added a 30s timeout on the endpoint using asyncio.wait_for().

error_message: KeyError: 'STRIPE_SECRET_KEY' / AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'startswith'
root_cause: Environment variable STRIPE_SECRET_KEY was set in .env but not passed to the Docker container — docker-compose env_file was pointing to .env.production which didn't exist on the staging server.
fix_applied: Added explicit env_file: .env to docker-compose.yml. Added startup validation in stripe_client.py that raises ValueError with clear message if key is missing. Added a CI/CD check that validates required env vars before deployment.

error_message: IndexError: list index out of range at ml/predict.py line 83
root_cause: ML model was trained on data with exactly 128 features but the inference pipeline was receiving 127 features after a schema change in the upstream data pipeline — a column was dropped without updating the feature list.
fix_applied: Added feature count assertion at inference time: assert len(features) == EXPECTED_FEATURES, f'Expected {EXPECTED_FEATURES}, got {len(features)}'. Added schema validation using pydantic model for inference inputs. Set up automated schema drift detection in the data pipeline.
